description: All 12 questions with their follow-ups in one session, largest first (generated by scripts/build-question-files.mjs; do not edit).

turns.prompt: Trace what the gentle-shell launcher does from the moment it is invoked until pi is running: how it chooses the agent home, how it finds the pi runtime and checks its version, what it does to a new or Gentle-owned home before launching, and how it makes pi load the Gentle Shell package (environment variables and arguments). Answer in English.

When exactly does the launcher take over gentle-pi instead of deferring to a declared package, what role does --package-root play in each home mode, and what does a take-over add to pi's arguments? Answer in English.

Explain how Gentle Shell's prompt-history feature works end to end: when capture is enabled, where and in what layout prompts are stored on disk, what a stored entry looks like, how a project's history gets seeded, and how the store is kept from growing into too many files. Answer in English.

When Gentle Shell runs with its default isolated home, do the prompt-history store and its transcript seeding follow that home? And when a prompt is deleted from the history selector, what exactly is written to hidden.json and how many entries does that file keep? Answer in English.

When the agent runs a shell command through the bash tool, how does Gentle Shell decide whether to allow it, ask for confirmation, or block it? Cover the order of the checks, which commands are recognized, the configuration that changes the outcome, how delegated child sessions differ, and what the YOLO session mode changes. Answer in English.

For a primary interactive session with no guardrail config files and no environment overrides, classify each of these commands and name the rule that decides it: (1) git push --force-with-lease origin main, (2) rm -rf ./build, (3) psql -c "DELETE FROM users", (4) git rebase main. Then say how (2) is handled in a delegated child session. Answer in English.

How does Gentle Shell handle telemetry? Describe both the per-response runtime usage reporting and the once-per-process telemetry nudge: what triggers each, what is sent and how, which environment variables disable each, and what happens when sending fails or is busy. Answer in English.

Suppose DO_NOT_TRACK=true (not 1) and CI is unset. Which of the two telemetry paths does Gentle Shell itself still run, and why? And what happens to a usage event that arrives while a previous runtime send is still in progress? Answer in English.

When an interactive Gentle Shell session is quit, Gentle Shell prints its own command for resuming the session. Why is pi's own resume hint not enough, and how does the information travel from the pi process to the code that prints the line? Describe what the printed command contains. Answer in English.

Suppose gentle-shell was started with --home /tmp/h in project A, the user then used /resume to open a session that belongs to project B, and quit normally. What form does the printed command take? What would be printed if the terminal had been closed (SIGHUP) instead? Answer in English.

In the Gentle Shell prompt editor, what does pressing Esc do while the agent is working, and what does it do while the agent is idle and the editor holds a non-empty draft? Which setting changes the working-state behavior, where is it stored and how is it resolved, and what happens to queued messages when a turn is aborted with Esc? Answer in English.

If GENTLE_PI_DOUBLE_ESC_CANCEL=on is set but the global policy file contains {"schema":"gentle-pi.double-esc-cancel/v1","policy":"on","note":"x"}, what is the effective policy and which source is reported? And if the user edits that file by hand mid-session, when does the Esc gate notice the change? Answer in English.

How does Gentle Shell's command palette work? Explain how it is opened, which commands it lists and how that list is built, how the list is filtered as the user types, and what happens when an entry is chosen. Answer in English.

Assume every Gentle extension is loaded. If the user types yolo into the palette's search box, which entries remain, in what order, and which entry is selected first? Explain using the ranking rules. Answer in English.

Gentle Shell can show subscription usage for connected providers. Which providers are supported, how does it obtain the usage data for each of them, when does it refresh, and how can another extension add usage support for a provider Gentle Shell does not know? Answer in English.

For NaN, how is the usage percentage of a model computed, including its rolling window? What happens to the whole snapshot if one metered model is missing tokensUsed? And what does the panel say for a provider outside the supported set? Answer in English.
Gentle Shell ships its own built-in provider for NaN Builders. How does that provider decide which models it offers, and how does it obtain the API key it sends? Answer in English.

Suppose the live /models call returns only the ids glm5.3-flash and kimi-k3. Which NaN models does pi list afterwards, with which context window, input types and maximum output tokens? And what would the list be if the call returned HTTP 500 instead? Answer in English.

Gentle Shell draws small percentage gauges in its bar and panels. How is such a gauge rendered: how many cells by default, which characters, how is the number of filled cells computed, and how is its color chosen? Answer in English.
With the default cell count, exactly what does the gauge show for 6%, for 94% and for null, and which color role does each one's filled part get? Answer in English.

Gentle Shell's prompt editor has an optional Vim mode. In its NORMAL-mode motion engine, how are numeric counts parsed and bounded, which keys switch to insert mode and where does each put the cursor, and how do gg and G behave with and without a count? Answer in English.

In a 3-line buffer with the cursor on the first line, what do the key sequences 5G, 1 0 j, and a bare 0 each do in that NORMAL-mode engine? Also, how does it split text into words for w, e and b? Answer in English.

Gentle Shell lets you save named visual profiles. Where are they stored, what does one profile contain, and what limits and validation rules apply when the file is read and when a profile is saved? Answer in English.

If one of ten stored visual profiles has its banner color set to "red", what does reading the profiles return, and can a new profile still be saved? What happens on an attempt to save a 65th profile into a valid file? Answer in English.
